newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Q1 GDP may have grown 9.0 pct--Rodriguez.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Q1 GDP may have grown 9.0 pct--Rodriguez.

text.p: The Economy Ministry's chief adviser Carlos Rodriguez said gross domestic product may have grown by up to nine percent in the first quarter.
"I would not be surprised if GDP grew eight or nine percent during the first quarter of the year," he told journalists Tuesday, according to the state-run news agency Telam.
"Recovery is not a myth," he added before an address to a banking conference in Buenos Aires, the private news agency DyN reported.

According to a commmunique issued by the Association of Argentine Banks, which reproduced extracts of his speech, Rodriguez said, "I deem GDP will grow this year six percent and inflation will not exceeed two percent. This means economic growth with monetary stability."
He said the recovery in GDP would be basically a consequence of a strong recovery of investments and an expansion of imports and exports.
Rodriguez added that according to preliminary data, the consumer price index will show no change in May.
